skill.name: container-orchestration
skill.description: Provides Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and Helm patterns for containerized application deployment.
skill.summary: Container deployment patterns for Docker, Kubernetes, Compose, and Helm workflows.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Dockerfile cleanup, Markdown code formatting, localhost health checks, and declarative Kubernetes examples. I confirmed insecure sample credentials in Compose and Kubernetes examples, a debug listener binding to all interfaces, and one semantic RBAC issue. No evidence found for prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or malicious installation behavior.

remediation.issue: Sample credentials appear in reusable Compose and Kubernetes examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace concrete passwords, API keys, and database URLs with placeholders that require user-supplied secret values before use.

remediation.issue: The Kubernetes RBAC example allows workloads to list secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Remove list access to secrets and grant only the minimum named secret access required by the application.

remediation.issue: The debug container example listens on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Mark the debug target as local-only, bind debug tooling to localhost where possible, and avoid exposing debug ports in shared clusters.

remediation.issue: The build helper can push images to a registry when requested.
remediation.suggestion: Document that pushes require explicit user approval and configured registry credentials, and keep the default behavior build-only.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Kubernetes Secret RBAC
semantic_findings.description: The production manifest example grants a workload role permission to get and list secrets in the namespace. Workloads should not list secrets unless there is a strict application requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The RBAC example explicitly includes resources configmaps and secrets with get and list verbs. This is a clear least-privilege issue in production-oriented Kubernetes guidance.

content.value_statement: Container setup often fails because Docker, Kubernetes, and Helm files drift from production needs. This skill provides reusable patterns for images, Compose stacks, manifests, charts, and image builds.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Dockerfile patterns with multi-stage builds, non-root users, health checks, and cache-aware dependency installation.
Provides Docker Compose examples for an app, PostgreSQL, Redis, optional worker, and optional reverse proxy services.
Supplies Kubernetes manifest examples for deployments, services, ingress, autoscaling, disruption budgets, network policy, RBAC, and jobs.
Outlines Helm chart structure, values files, helpers, deployment templates, and release configuration patterns.
Includes a shell script pattern for building Docker images and optionally pushing them to a registry.
limitations: Examples require review before production because sample secrets and defaults must be replaced.
It does not validate manifests against a live cluster unless the user runs external tools.
The patterns focus on common web services and may need changes for stateful or regulated workloads.
The build script assumes Docker, Git, registry access, and local credentials are already configured.

use_cases.title: Create a service container baseline
use_cases.description: Generate a Dockerfile and Compose stack for a new web service with health checks and dependency services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kubernetes production manifests
use_cases.description: Build deployment, service, ingress, autoscaling, disruption budget, network policy, and job examples for a release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Helm packaging
use_cases.description: Plan a chart layout with environment values, templates, helpers, resource settings, and release conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a production image baseline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Dockerfile pattern for my Python web service. Include dependency caching, a non-root user, health checks, and clear places for app-specific changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Compose stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose plan for an app with PostgreSQL and Redis. Include health checks, named volumes, service dependencies, and notes for replacing sample secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Review Kubernetes readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Kubernetes deployment plan for production readiness. Focus on security context, probes, resources, autoscaling, disruption budget, network policy, and RBAC scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Helm release
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced chart design for repeatable environments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Helm chart structure for this service. Include values organization, helper naming, environment overrides, secret handling, autoscaling settings, and release validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need a Docker baseline for a FastAPI service.
output_examples.output: A staged container plan with dependency caching, non-root execution, runtime environment settings, a health check, exposed port guidance, and notes for app-specific files.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare Kubernetes manifests for a web app.
output_examples.output: A deployment checklist covering namespace, config, secrets, service, ingress, resources, probes, security context, autoscaling, network policy, and release safety checks.

output_examples.input: Create a Helm packaging approach for staging and production.
output_examples.output: A chart structure proposal with values files, helper naming, environment overrides, autoscaling settings, and safe release commands.

best_practices: Replace all sample credentials and URLs before using generated files in shared or production environments.
Run container scanners and Kubernetes policy checks before applying manifests or pushing images.
Keep build, deployment, and secret-management steps explicit so users approve external commands.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample passwords, API keys, or database URLs into production files.
Do not expose debug listeners or database ports beyond trusted local development networks.
Do not grant workloads broad permissions to list secrets unless the application strictly requires it.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy workloads automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and scripts, but deployment requires explicit user action and configured tools.

faq.question: Can it create Docker and Kubernetes files for a new service?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide Dockerfiles, Compose stacks, Kubernetes manifests, and Helm chart structure.

faq.question: Are the included examples production-ready as written?
faq.answer: No. Users must replace sample secrets, review network exposure, and validate policies before production use.

faq.question: Does it support Helm?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes chart structure, values organization, helper templates, and release configuration guidance.

faq.question: What tools does the build script require?
faq.answer: The script expects Docker, Git, optional registry credentials, and a local project with a Dockerfile.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled with this skill?
faq.answer: Use a secret manager or Kubernetes Secret references, and never keep real credentials in templates or images.
